recentItems.title: Do we want AI to become the next pop icon? | Andrae Alexander | TEDxPrincetonU
recentItems.description:
Grammy Winner, Dr. Andrae Alexander Ph.D. sheds light on the potential negative effects of allowing AI, in the form of Virtual Artists and generative song creation tools, to replace the role of human songwriters and artists, and offers the C.O.P.S. Framework as a means by which to create a win-win social environment for corporations, creatives in the music industry, and society at large. 

Andrae Alexander, Ph.D., is a Grammy Award-winning composer, music industry scholar, faculty member at the University of Southern California, and veteran of both the Marine Corps and Navy. As an advocate for music creatives, Andrae serves on the board of the Songwriters of North America (SONA) and the Unclaimed Royalties Oversight Committee of the Mechanical Licensing Collective (MLC). Dr. Alexander has over 20 years of music industry experience and implements strategies to ensure that the next generation of music creatives are able to have access to resources that assist them in creating the songs that act as the soundtracks to our lives. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Credibility Is the New Social Capital | Vaishnavi Bhupalam | TEDxSt Pauls College
recentItems.description: Vaishnavi Bhupalam, CEO of Kinfluence Media, explores how credibility and trust have become essential assets in today's digital and influencer-driven world. Her talk examines how authenticity, transparency, and meaningful relationships shape public perception and influence. She highlights why genuine connections and consistent communication matter more than mere visibility, encouraging audiences to build trust and use their influence responsibly. Vaishnavi Bhupalam is the Founder of Kinfluence Media, a seven-figure marketing agency that helps founders build influential personal brands and enables businesses to scale through influencer marketing. In less than 10 months, she has grown Kinfluence Media into a team of 10 and worked with more than 50 founders and brands across industries. Her entrepreneurial journey began after facing hundreds of rejections, an experience that taught her to stop waiting for opportunities and start creating them. Vaishnavi has been featured in multiple media publications and appeared in more than 10 YouTube interviews. Today, she is passionate about helping individuals and businesses leverage the internet to build credibility, create opportunities, and achieve financial independence. Her work sits at the intersection of personal branding, digital credibility, entrepreneurship, and influencer marketing. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What walls teach us about human connection | Leon Rainbow | TEDxCapeMay
recentItems.description:
What if the health of a community could be measured not just by statistics, but by its stories, its creativity, and the walls that surround us? After nearly three decades painting murals in neighborhoods across America, Leon Rainbow has discovered that public art is more than decoration—it reveals a community’s pulse. Through powerful stories of transformation, recovery, and collaboration, he invites us to see walls not as barriers, but as mirrors reflecting who we are and who we can become. This talk will challenge audiences to recognize creativity as a vital sign of thriving communities and inspire them to become active participants in shaping the places they call home. Leon Rainbow is a nationally recognized muralist, public artist, educator, and founder of Jersey Fresh Jam, one of New Jersey’s longest-running celebrations of hip-hop culture. For more than 25 years, he has transformed schools, neighborhoods, parks, recovery centers, and public spaces into vibrant works of art that celebrate identity, resilience, and belonging.

Beginning as a graffiti writer, Leon discovered that walls could do more than display art—they could tell stories, amplify overlooked voices, and bring communities together. Today, his collaborative murals are created through conversations with residents, students, and organizations, ensuring each project reflects the people it serves.

A proud member of the Quechan Tribe, Leon believes creativity is one of the strongest indicators of a healthy community. Through his artwork, teaching, and public speaking, he inspires others to see public art as a catalyst for lasting transformation. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Sound of Belonging | Jessica Gallagher-Steuver | TEDxClevelandStateUniversity
recentItems.description:
Singing is a joyful, human activity. It can also be incredibly vulnerable. Jessica Gallagher-Steuver, conductor of Windsong, Cleveland's Feminist Chorus, will highlight the unique sense of belonging that can come from group singing in a radically affirming environment. Jessica L. Gallagher-Steuver is a music educator, choral conductor, performer and clinician. She is a visiting assistant professor of music education at Baldwin Wallace Conservatory and has taught at Cleveland State University and Case Western Reserve University.

Gallagher-Steuver is artistic director of Windsong, Cleveland's feminist chorus, a nonprofit organization focused on music and social justice. In 2025, she founded the  Journal of Queer Choral Studies, the official academic publication of GALA Choruses. Her research focuses on queer studies in music education, the social and emotional benefits of choral singing, vocal health in older adults and community music-making. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Udržitelnost jako přirozená cesta | Martin Štangl | TEDxOlomouc
recentItems.description:
Udržitelnost jako přirozená cesta, ne ideologie.
Šéfkuchař Martin Štangl ukazuje, že skutečně udržitelná gastronomie nevzniká díky certifikátům, ale díky každodenním rozhodnutím v práci se sezónní surovinou, v péči o tým i v dlouhodobých vztazích s dodavateli. Restaurace je podle něj ekosystém, který musí fungovat ekonomicky, lidsky i ekologicky. Udržitelnost není cíl, ale cesta. A začít se dá kdykoliv. Hned po škole prošel několika předními pražskými restauracemi, nejvíce ho však ovlivnila zkušenost v michelinské La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise, kde se během osmi let vypracoval až na pozici sous-chefa. V roce 2015 dostal příležitost podílet se na otevření karlínské Esky a z pozice šéfkuchaře zde naplno rozvíjet své představy o moderní české kuchyni, která respektuje tradici i sezonu. Od léta 2023 stojí v čele zážitkové restaurace Štangl, kde hosté ochutnávají to, co právě nabízí příroda. Od prosince 2025 je restaurace držitelem jedné michelinské hvězdy a také zelené hvězdy, která se uděluje podnikům za důsledný přístup k udržitelnosti. 

Martin má rád bylinky – především ty divoké –, staré odrůdy i zapomenuté recepty našich (pra)babiček. Velkou část inspirace nachází v přírodě – za tou se před lety odstěhoval z Prahy 1 na Sázavu, kde společně se svou ženou vede penzion. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

One person. One action. One small moment that you might forget— but someone else never does. I used to think making an impact meant doing something big. Something people would notice. But one day, something very small changed the way I saw it.

recentItems.title: It’s Not About the Glass | Rev Fr Dr Joseph T C | TEDxSt Pauls College
recentItems.description: Rev. Fr. Dr. Joseph T. C., Chairman of ST PAULS COLLEGE, shares a thought-provoking perspective on how our outlook shapes the way we experience life. His talk explores how we often focus on what we lack rather than appreciating what we have, reminding us that happiness and fulfilment depend more on our attitude than on our circumstances. Through this powerful message, he encourages audiences to shift their perspective, practise gratitude, and discover the deeper meaning behind everyday experiences. Rev. Fr. Joseph T. C. is an author, visionary, and humble servant leader who has dedicated his life to the service of humanity. His journey reflects a deep commitment to education, compassion, human values, and holistic development. Known for his simplicity and grounded nature, he believes that true leadership is rooted in service, empathy, and making a meaningful difference in the lives of others. Through his work and writings, he continues to inspire people to look beyond themselves and contribute to the greater good.
